name: Fallout: New Vegas
notes: Gamebryo DX9. The path that actually ran on this Mac was Wine builtin ddraw/d3d9 → wined3d → OpenGL (same class as Army Men RTS), not this JSON's DXVK layer. MEASURED 2026-09-11 with lsof on the live FalloutNV.exe: it loads d3d9.dll, wined3d.dll and opengl32.dll from the running Wine tree's i386-windows and renders through AppleMetalOpenGLRenderer — no dxgi, no d3d11, nothing from the DXVK payload, which is deployed on every launch and never opened (DXVK ships no d3d9). Identical module set whether it runs alone or straight after another game. The declared dxvk layer therefore buys nothing here; changing it is a separate question because the layer also decides the launch path (dxvk/dxmt → steam -applaunch on the frankea tree, d3dmetal → direct EXE on the game tree), and that has not been measured for this title. See wyn-handovers/FINDING-20260911-taskb-legs.md. Status stays guessed. Steam launches FalloutNVLauncher.exe; prefer FalloutNV.exe with SteamAppId=22380. Keep vsync on — Gamebryo physics breaks at high FPS. This is New Vegas, not Fallout 4. Prefs live in Documents\My Games\FalloutNV.
